keyVerseText: Which was the son of Joanna, which was the son of Rhesa, which was the son of Zorobabel, which was the son of Salathiel, which was the son of Neri,
rootMeaning: The name Ἰωαννᾶς (Iōannâs) is a Greek form derived from Ἰωάννης (Iōánnēs), which corresponds to the Hebrew יוֹחָנָן (Yochanan). This root name means 'Yahweh is gracious' or 'God is gracious,' highlighting a divine attribute of grace. Understanding Ἰωαννᾶς as a variant of Ἰωάννης enriches the common English name 'John' by emphasizing the gracious character of God embedded in the original Hebrew context.
usageInScripture: The word Ἰωαννᾶς appears only once in the New Testament, specifically in Luke 3:27, where it is translated as 'Joanna' or 'Joannas,' identifying an Israelite individual. This singular occurrence limits its range but firmly establishes it as a proper noun referencing a person within a genealogical or historical context. The consistent translation as a personal name underlines its role in connecting individuals to their heritage and to God's unfolding plan.
theologicalSignificance: Theologically, the name Ἰωαννᾶς, rooted in the meaning 'God is gracious,' reminds believers of the foundational truth that God's grace is central to human identity and salvation history. As a name borne by an Israelite in Luke's genealogy, it points to God's ongoing covenant faithfulness to His people through generations. Recognizing the divine grace implicit in this name encourages Christians to see their own lives as recipients of God's unmerited favor, which culminates in the person and work of Jesus Christ. Thus, Ἰωαννᾶς serves as a subtle but profound testament to the grace that undergirds all biblical narratives and the Christian faith.
keyVerseReflection: Luke 3:27 traces a lineage stating, 'Which was the son of Joanna...' and here Ἰωαννᾶς identifies a specific ancestor within the genealogy. This name not only situates the individual historically but also conveys the theological depth of divine grace extending through generations. The presence of Ἰωαννᾶς in this verse invites readers to reflect on God's gracious provision and faithfulness in the unfolding story of salvation, linking personal identity with divine purpose.
